pageStructure: Sticky dark header (Elementor sticky:top, offset 0, all breakpoints, ~87px): left = logo mark (4-square grid) + wordmark; centre-left = country switcher Moldova / România stacked two-line with active state in white and inactive in grey; right = horizontal nav (mega-menu on hover), a compact language chip (RO/RU/EN via TranslatePress), a yellow pill phone button, and a 3-bar hamburger SVG that opens a push off-canvas panel

Hero: full-viewport-width image band ~960px tall, built as an Elementor Slides/Swiper widget with a SINGLE slide (transition:fade, speed 500, navigation:none — i.e. functionally a static hero). Content block is bottom-LEFT aligned (h-position:left, v-position:bottom), sitting on a dark translucent scrim over an architectural render: serif display title (Prata), 3–4 lines of intro text, one solid yellow CTA button

Key-numbers band: oversized numerals set at 90px Space Grotesk in pale blue (#CDE7F2) — number on top, small caption underneath — paired with a supporting photo. Reads as an editorial stat row rather than a boxed infographic

Icon spec strip on light grey (#EAEAE9): 4 Elementor image-box widgets, each a thin-line outline icon above a centred two-line caption (apartment size range, height regime, parking count, etc.). Very airy, generous vertical padding

Location / setting section: left-aligned h3 (Space Grotesk 38px/600) + a hairline 1px full-width divider immediately under the heading + a body paragraph column constrained to ~50% width + a large photo

APARTMENT PICKER SECTION (the core, ~2400px tall, custom shortcode inside an Elementor container): heading + 1px divider + intro paragraph, then (a) a filter tab row, (b) a responsive card grid of 22 unit plans with a progressive-disclosure 'show more' button, (c) TWO interactive floor-plate image maps below the grid — one for the single-staircase block type, one for the two-staircase block type
Architecture section: heading + hairline divider + text, then a wide photo band (ventilated façade / material story)
Efficiency section: mirrored layout — photo first, then heading + divider + text (alternating left/right rhythm against the previous section)

Parking downloads: an intro heading followed by 5 identical rows, one per block — block label, a 'download plan' sub-label, and a download icon, each linking to a per-block basement PDF (Subsol-Bloc-1..5.pdf)
Small CTA strip: one line of text + a brochure-download button
Full-bleed image band (single image widget, no text) used as a visual breather before the form
Contact block (footer_form_block1): heading + short paragraph + Contact Form 7 form (name/phone/email/message, GDPR checkbox, invisible reCAPTCHA v3, piped to amoCRM)
Footer (raw HTML widget): logo, address, social icons (FB / YouTube / Instagram), department-by-department phone + email columns, privacy / terms links

Persistent floating layer: a 65px circular navy-gradient phone FAB (fixed bottom-right, 20px inset, 65px radius, box-shadow 0 19px 38px rgba(34,36,43,.3)) plus the JivoSite chat launcher just below it
layoutPatterns: Single-column editorial stack: alternating text-left/image-right then image-left/text-right, no sidebars, sections separated by background colour (white → #EAEAE9 light grey → white) rather than by borders
Signature 'heading + hairline' unit: an h3 with a 1px solid divider directly beneath it, width driven by the container, used consistently to open almost every section
Text columns are deliberately narrowed (~50–60% of the container) while images go edge-to-edge or near-edge — a strong asymmetry that creates whitespace on one side
Oversized numerals as a layout element (90px Space Grotesk stat figures, 35px area figures on unit cards) — numbers, not photos, carry the visual weight in the data sections

Unit cards are unstyled and un-carded: a 1px black hairline rectangle around the plan drawing on a plain background, with the metadata OUTSIDE and BELOW the frame (area figure large, room-count label small, left-aligned). No shadow, no radius, no fill — a deliberately drawing-like, architectural presentation
Card grid uses Foundation-style .col-3 (4-up desktop, collapses to 1-up under 1024px); 8 cards visible on load and the rest hidden, revealed 8 at a time
Filter tabs are a flex row of pale-blue (#CDE7F2) full-bleed rectangular pills with 25px column-gap, 45px line-height, 20px type — flat, no radius, wrapping to a stacked full-width list on mobile
Parking downloads laid out as five identical horizontal rows (label / sub-label / icon) — a table-like rhythm without a table
Zero rounded corners anywhere in the content (border-radius 3px on buttons only, 65px only on the phone FAB) — the whole page commits to square geometry
Elementor container (flex) layout with breakpoints at 767 / 880 / 1024; content max-width around 1140–1200px
animations: IMPORTANT BASELINE FINDING: this page has almost NO scroll-triggered motion. Four animation libraries are loaded (animate.css from WP Mega Menu Pro, a Flatsome-derived animations.css with fadeIn/fadeInUp/fadeInLeft/fadeInRight/fadeInUpBig/bounceIn*/flipInX/flipInY/rotateIn* keyframes, Dynamic-Content-for-Elementor animations.css, and TheP lus with a pt-plus-reveal keyframe) but a live DOM audit found 0 elements carrying .animated / .elementor-invisible / any entrance class. Everything below is the motion that ACTUALLY runs.

Sticky header: Elementor jquery.sticky, sticky:top, sticky_offset 0, sticky_effects_offset 0, enabled on desktop+tablet+mobile — it simply pins, with no shrink, no colour change, no hide-on-scroll-down. (The theme has commented-out code for an .active class after 500px of scroll — the shrink-on-scroll idea was built and then abandoned.)

Off-canvas menu (UAEL): type 'push' from the LEFT — the entire page body slides right rather than the panel overlaying it; body scroll is locked while open (uael-offcanvas-scroll-disable), an inset shadow rims the panel edge, close icon pinned top-right of the panel
Mega-menu dropdown: WP Mega Menu Pro in on-hover mode with the 'zoom-inout' animation — the panel scales in/out from its trigger on hover rather than sliding
INTERACTIVE FLOOR-PLATE MAP — pageload: Image Map Pro is configured with pageload_animation:'fall-down', so on first paint the unit polygons drop into place over the plan drawing

INTERACTIVE FLOOR-PLATE MAP — idle: glowing_shapes is enabled, driving a 'ShapeGlowAnimation' keyframe (linear, 1.5s, infinite) that pulses a soft glow layer behind each hotspot as the resting affordance

INTERACTIVE FLOOR-PLATE MAP — hover: the hovered polygon's fill transitions from fully transparent to rgba(255,255,255,0.4) — a white wash that lights up exactly that apartment's footprint on the plan. Transition is `all .15s cubic-bezier(.55,0,.1,1)` (a fast ease-in-out-quad-ish curve), applied to every shape

INTERACTIVE FLOOR-PLATE MAP — tooltip: a white card fades AND transforms in over 0.2s cubic-bezier(.55,0,.1,1) (transition-property: transform, opacity), anchored to the shape with a CSS triangle arrow, 0px radius, 10px padding, box-shadow 0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,.3). It contains a 2-row 'squares' grid: row 1 = room-count heading + area heading; row 2 = two half-width images side by side (flat 2D unit plan + 3D isometric cut-away render)

INTERACTIVE FLOOR-PLATE MAP — viewport: the map is wrapped in .imp-zoom-outer-wrap > .imp-translate-wrap > .imp-zoom-wrap, so pan/zoom transforms are available (zoom level 2 stored in the editor config); an .imp-ui slot exists for zoom controls though it is rendered empty here

Unit-card image hover: transform: scale(1.125) on the plan drawing with `all .5s ease` — a slow, generous zoom inside the hairline frame (the frame clips via overflow:hidden so the drawing grows within its box)

Filter pill hover/active: background and colour cross-fade over `all .5s ease` (pale blue #CDE7F2 → navy #142A3D with white text on the active tab); the active class is moved by JS, so the previous tab fades out as the new one fades in
Filter switching itself is INSTANT — matching cards get a .hide class, non-matching get height:0 + visibility:hidden. There is no FLIP/reflow animation, no stagger, no fade

'Show more' reveal: clicking the button strips .hide_planemetr from the next batch of 8 cards, which snaps them from height:0 to auto — again instant, no expand transition. When the last batch is shown the button hides itself

Unit detail popup: clicking a card's plan image adds .active to a `position:fixed` full-screen panel (z-index 1010) that flips opacity 0→1 and visibility hidden→visible. `transition:all` is declared with NO duration, so it appears abruptly. Opening also adds .hide to the site header and .active to a fixed close button; closing reverses both

Inside the unit popup: a slick carousel (.plan_images1) — 1 slide, infinite, arrows on, autoplay off, speed 800ms, swipeToSlide, adaptiveHeight (so the container height animates as slides of different aspect ratio come in)

Every unit card also carries its own mini slick carousel (.slider_apartamente1): 1 slide, arrows, speed 800ms, swipeToSlide, adaptiveHeight — 22 slick instances initialise on this page (44 .slick-initialized nodes counted live)
Hero: Swiper with transition 'fade' at 500ms — but only one slide exists, so the crossfade never fires. No Ken Burns, no parallax, no video

Sibling templates in the same design system (homepage/listing) add: a 4-up autoplay carousel (speed 800, autoplaySpeed 4000, slidesToShow 4/4), a centre-mode carousel with 20% peek at slidesToShow 1.5, a 2-up and a 3-up autoplay carousel, custom prev/next arrow elements that scale(1.05) on hover over 0.5s, a slick `beforeChange` handler that drives a PROGRESS BAR by animating background-size from 0→100% as you advance through slides, and project cards that transition from grayscale(1) to grayscale(0) on hover over 0.5s

A bouncing scroll-down arrow keyframe exists (`bounce2`: translateY 0 → -30px → -15px → 0, 2s ease infinite) but it is dead code on this template — the property name is misspelled ('animationÑ') and it is homepage-scoped anyway
Button hover: 0.3s transition on the yellow (#FFD63E) fill; image-box icons carry a 0.3s transition-duration
Right-click / image-drag are suppressed globally ($('img').mousedown(return false)) — an anti-copy measure that also kills drag affordance
Floating phone FAB is completely static — no pulse, no ring, no hover growth (transform matrix is identity, animation:none). Only the JivoSite launcher animates, and that is third-party chrome

TheP lus pre-loader plugin (plus-pre-loader.min.js + plus-pre-loader-extra-transition.min.js, with ~30 loader keyframes and a page-transition module) is enqueued on the page but no preloader element is present in the DOM — the page-transition capability is loaded and unused
result.typography: ["Two-family system with a third leaking in. Display/hero: PRATA — a high-contrast Didone-ish serif, used at 25px on mobile hero with letter-spacing 1.5px and line-height 35px, scaling up on desktop; it is the only serif and it carries the 'premium' signal.","Workhorse: SPACE GROTESK (400/500/600) for all section headings, UI, numerals and buttons. Section h3 = 38px / weight 600 / letter-spacing normal / colour #000. Big stat numerals = 90px / weight 400 / #CDE7F2. Unit-card area figure = 35px / weight 500 / line-height 1, with the room-count label right under it at 18px / weight 400 in #12100B. Filter tabs = 20px / weight 700. Buttons = 14px / weight 500, no uppercase, no letter-spacing. 'Show more' button = 24px / weight 500.","Body copy runs at 16px in the default system stack in places (Open Sans is enqueued and used for some legacy blocks), so the body text is the least designed layer.","Character: no uppercase transforms in the current template (the older stylesheet had text-transform:uppercase on unit labels and it was overridden to 'none'), tight-to-normal tracking, headings set flush left, and a very large display-to-body size jump (90px vs 16px) that does most of the hierarchical work.","Five families are actually requested over the wire — Prata, Space Grotesk, Open Sans, Roboto and Montserrat — which is more than the design uses."]
result.imageryStyle: ["Three distinct image registers, kept visually separate and never mixed inside one component. (1) EXTERIOR RENDERS: warm-toned, near-photoreal CGI of the buildings in daylight with mature landscaping and sky, used full-bleed at large heights, always with a dark translucent scrim only where text sits, never a global overlay. (2) TECHNICAL DRAWINGS: furnished 2D apartment plans and full floor-plate plans, rendered as light grey/white line drawings with soft colour accents (teal for water/glass, green for planting), presented inside a 1px black hairline frame with object-fit:scale-down and object-position:top so the drawing floats with air around it and never crops. (3) 3D ISOMETRIC CUT-AWAYS: white-model axonometric views of the same unit, furnished, no ceiling — these appear only inside the map tooltip, paired 50/50 with the flat plan.","Pairing the flat plan and the 3D cut-away side by side in one tooltip is the single most effective imagery decision on the page — it answers 'what does this shape actually feel like' in one hover.","Aspect ratios are not normalised: unit plans use max-height 400px (600px above 2000px viewport) with scale-down, so tall and wide plans both fit without distortion, at the cost of an irregular grid rhythm.","No duotone, no colour grading, no masking, no image-shape play — imagery is presented straight. Project-listing templates elsewhere on the site do use grayscale→colour on hover.","179 images on the page, 84 lazy-loaded."]
result.buildingOrUnitPicker: "YES — but it is a FLOOR-PLATE unit picker, not a building/block/floor selector. Built with Image Map Pro for WordPress 5.6.9 (plugin path /image-map-pro-wordpress/, JS image-map-pro.min.js). MECHANICS: two separate maps are placed one under the other, each corresponding to a block typology — map A (id 16, source image obshii.jpg, 1965x1094) has 8 hotspots and is labelled as the single-staircase floor plan; map B (id 6418, source satul-pla-scaled.jpg, 2560x1094) has 14 hotspots and is the two-staircase floor plan. Each hotspot is an SVG <polygon class='imp-shape imp-shape-poly'> whose points are stored as percentage coordinates against the natural image size, so the overlay scales with the raster plan; shapes are titled by area ('91.85', '46-35', '73.20-2' etc.). STRUCTURE: .imp-wrap > .imp-ui (empty zoom-control slot) > .imp-zoom-outer-wrap > .imp-translate-wrap > .imp-zoom-wrap, containing an .imp-image-backgrounds-container of per-shape crop layers plus the SVG shape container at z-index 2 — pan/zoom is architecturally available (editor zoom level 2) but no visible controls are exposed here. RESTING STATE: hotspots are fully transparent — the plan looks like a plain image, with only the configured glow pulse (ShapeGlowAnimation, linear 1.5s infinite) hinting at interactivity. ON HOVER: the polygon fill transitions to rgba(255,255,255,0.4) over 0.15s cubic-bezier(.55,0,.1,1), washing that one apartment white against the grey plan, and a white tooltip card fades+transforms in over 0.2s with the same curve — 0px radius, 10px padding, arrow pointer, shadow 0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,.3). The tooltip holds a small responsive grid: room count and area as two stacked headings, then the flat 2D unit plan and a 3D isometric cut-away render side by side at sq-col-lg-6 each. ON CLICK: nothing — no action is configured on any shape, so the hotspot is purely a hover-reveal. STATES SHOWN: room count, area, plan, render — and NOTHING ELSE. There is no free/reserved/sold status, no price (the markup has a 'Valorea:' row with an empty .plan__rate span), no floor number, no block number, no orientation, no availability count, no colour coding, no legend, no deep link. Alongside the maps sits a parallel, non-spatial picker: a filter-tab row (all / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 rooms, plain <li data-role='button' data-filter='...'>) driving a 22-card grid of the same units, 8 shown initially with a 'show more' button revealing 8 at a time; clicking a card's plan image opens a fixed full-screen detail panel (z-index 1010) split left = room count / area / price row / VAT note, right = a slick carousel of the plan images, dismissed by a fixed black close square. The two pickers are not linked — hovering a hotspot does not highlight the corresponding card, and there is no floor or block navigation anywhere. Parking is handled entirely outside the picker as five static per-block basement PDFs (Subsol-Bloc-1..5.pdf)."
whatMakesItFeelPremium: Serif display + geometric-grotesque UI pairing (Prata over Space Grotesk) — one high-contrast serif carries the brand voice while a neutral grotesque does all the functional work. Cheap developer sites use one font for everything.
Committing to square geometry: 0px radius on tooltips, cards, filter pills and popups; the only radii on the page are a 3px button and the circular FAB. Sharp corners read architectural.

Presenting unit plans as DRAWINGS, not products: a 1px black hairline frame, object-fit:scale-down, object-position:top, no shadow, no card fill, metadata typeset outside and below the frame. It looks like a plan sheet, not an e-commerce tile.
Oversized numerals as the hierarchy device — 90px stat figures in pale blue, 35px area figures on cards, with the descriptive label demoted to 18px underneath. The number is the headline.
The heading + 1px hairline divider pattern repeated at every section opening — a single cheap detail applied with total consistency, which is what makes it read as a system rather than a page.

Restrained palette anchored on deep navy #142A3D with a single saturated accent (#FFD63E yellow) and two neutral grounds (#EAEAE9 warm grey, #CDE7F2 pale blue). The accent appears only on CTAs and the area figure inside the popup — scarcity is what makes it feel considered.
The hover tooltip pairing a flat 2D plan with a 3D isometric cut-away of the same unit, side by side — this is the highest-value idea on the whole site and is cheap to reproduce.

A fast, tight motion curve used consistently on the map: cubic-bezier(.55,0,.1,1) at 0.15s for the shape and 0.2s for the tooltip. Short and snappy on the precision interaction, while the decorative hover (card image scale 1.125) is deliberately slow at 0.5s. Different speeds for different intents.
Alternating image-left / image-right section rhythm with narrowed text columns (~50–60%) against near-full-bleed imagery — the asymmetric whitespace does more than any decoration would.
Section separation by background colour blocks rather than rules or borders.
Progressive disclosure on the unit grid (8 → 8 → 8) so the page never dumps 22 plans at once.
Per-block basement parking as individual downloadable PDFs rather than one undifferentiated brochure — a small signal of thoroughness that buyers notice.
The push-style off-canvas menu (page slides right, body scroll locked) rather than a modal overlay — a more physical, considered transition than a fade.
A permanent contact affordance (navy gradient circular phone FAB with a very soft 19px/38px shadow) that never competes with content because it carries no animation.
weaknesses: Almost no scroll motion despite four animation libraries being shipped. animate.css, a Flatsome-derived animations.css (fadeInUp, fadeInLeft, bounceIn, flipInX, rotateIn…), Dynamic-Content-for-Elementor animations.css and TheP lus's pt-plus-reveal are all downloaded; a live DOM audit found zero elements using any of them. The page pays the full weight and delivers none of the effect. For a client who explicitly wants 'many cool animations', this reference is a cautionary example, not a model.

Hotspots are completely invisible at rest — transparent fill, no outline, no numbering, no legend, no 'hover to explore' hint. A visitor has no reason to move the mouse over the plan. Do NOT copy this; give hotspots a visible resting state.

No availability data at all. No sold/reserved/free states, no colour coding, no counts, no floor selector, no block selector, no orientation/compass, no view direction. The 'price' row exists in the markup but renders empty ('Valorea:' followed by a blank span) — a broken-looking field on every single unit.

No real building or block picker. Five blocks × six floors are described in text, but there is no way to pick a block, pick a floor, or see a façade/site plan with clickable volumes. Both maps are single generic floor plates reused for the whole development.

Hotspots have no click action — hovering is the entire interaction. On touch devices this degrades badly, and the tooltip card overflows the viewport edge on narrow screens (observed clipped off the left edge at ~500px wide).

The two pickers are disconnected: hovering a hotspot does not highlight the matching grid card and vice versa, so the same 22 units are presented twice with no relationship between the representations.
No URL state anywhere — filter selection and the open unit popup are not routable, so a specific apartment cannot be linked, shared or bookmarked, and back/forward do nothing.

The unit popup opens with no animation: `transition:all` with no duration, opacity and visibility toggled via !important. It also uses hardcoded percentage offsets (`top:24%!important`, and a mobile override to 12%) for the close button, which is fragile at every intermediate viewport.
Filter switching and 'show more' are instant DOM class flips (height:0 + visibility:hidden) with no FLIP, stagger or fade — the grid jumps.

Accessibility is poor and would need to be rebuilt, not copied: filter tabs are <li data-role='button'> with click listeners only (not focusable, no roles, no aria-selected); the popup is not a dialog (no role, no focus trap, no Esc handler, no aria-modal); SVG polygons have no accessible name or keyboard path; a global $('img').mousedown(false) anti-copy handler blocks image dragging.

Fragile JS: a single close listener bound to document.querySelector('.close__popup') and a close handler that reads .popup_block.active without a null guard; the 'show more' logic tracks visibility with a bespoke .hide_planemetr class rather than a data model.

Very heavy and dated stack: WordPress 6.0.3, Elementor 3.7.8 / Pro 3.7.7, ~50 CSS and ~50 JS requests, jQuery + jQuery UI + jQuery Migrate + Modernizr, slick + slick-lightbox + iosslider + magnific-popup + bxslider + colorbox (five separate carousel/lightbox libraries), 179 images, 22 slick instances initialised on one page, plus Google Maps and two reCAPTCHA loads.
A whole Swiper hero for one static slide — the fade transition is configured and can never fire.
Five webfont families requested (Prata, Space Grotesk, Open Sans, Roboto, Montserrat) for a two-family design.

Messy CSS with duplicate and typo'd declarations shipped to production (`paddingx`, `overflowx`, `backgroundx`, `animationÑ`, `background` declared twice on the same rule), and heavy !important usage.
An asset is hot-linked from a different domain (the popup close icon loads from satulgerman.md), which will break if that site changes.
Two dead capabilities are shipped: TheP lus preloader + page-transition JS is enqueued with no preloader element in the DOM, and a bouncing scroll-cue keyframe exists but is disabled by a typo.
Layout rhythm is monotonous below the picker — heading, divider, text, image, repeated; no full-bleed break, no sticky side rail, no pinned section, nothing to reset the eye across a ~9200px page.
Floor plans are raster images (a 2560px JPEG scaled down) rather than SVG, so the plan itself blurs on high-DPI screens and the hotspot geometry is locked to one bitmap.
result.techStack: "WordPress 6.0.3 (Hello Elementor parent theme + a heavily customised 'hello-theme-child-master' child theme) built page-by-page in Elementor 3.7.8 with Elementor Pro 3.7.7 (flex-container experiment on, page-transitions experiment on). Plugin layer: Image Map Pro for WordPress 5.6.9 (the interactive floor-plate picker), Ultimate Addons for Elementor 1.36.8 (push off-canvas menu, particle-background module loaded), TheP lus Elementor Addon 5.1.0 (pre-loader + page-transition JS, per-post compiled CSS/JS bundles), Dynamic Content for Elementor 2.6.1 (raw-PHP widgets, dynamic backgrounds/visibility, its own animations.css), WP Mega Menu Pro 2.1.6 (on-hover mega menu with zoom-in/out, bundles animate.css, bxSlider, Colorbox), Filter Everything Pro 1.6.5 + Select2 (used on the projects archive), TranslatePress 2.3.8 (RO/RU/EN), Contact Form 7 5.6.4 with an amoCRM lead-generation bridge and reCAPTCHA v3, All in One SEO Pro, Redux 4.3.19. Front-end libraries: jQuery 3.6.0 + jQuery Migrate + jQuery UI (core/mouse/slider/draggable + touch-punch), Modernizr, Swiper (via Elementor Slides), slick-carousel 1.9.0 + slick-lightbox 0.2.12 from cdnjs (the custom apartment sliders), jquery.iosslider, Magnific Popup, js.cookie, Waypoints 4.0.2, imagesLoaded, Google Maps JS API with Places, Font Awesome 5.7.2/5.15.3, Linearicons, Eicons, Iconsmind. Fonts from Google Fonts: Prata, Space Grotesk, Open Sans, Roboto, Montserrat. Third-party: JivoSite live chat. Server: nginx, no CDN in front of the origin, no build pipeline — CSS/JS are per-post generated files under /wp-content/uploads/. No React/Vue/Next, no GSAP, no Lenis, no Framer Motion, no Locomotive, no ScrollTrigger, no Three.js/WebGL anywhere."

pageStructure: UTILITY TOP BAR (charcoal #3A3839, 45px, class lqd-hide-onstuck): row of 4 circular orange messenger icons (Messenger/Viber/Telegram/WhatsApp) at far left, two phone numbers in white semibold at far right. Collapses away the moment the header sticks.

MAIN HEADER (light grey band, ~104px, Elementor header builder + Liquid 'Hub' theme): 3D isometric orange logo mark + two-line silver wordmark at left; right cluster = solid-orange primary CTA ('choose an apartment' -> /proiecte-curente/), dark secondary CTA with an icon (contact, opens a Lity modal), TranslatePress RO/EN/RU select, and a 3-bar burger that opens a FULLSCREEN overlay menu. Header is 'smart sticky': it slides out on scroll-down and slides back in on scroll-up.

HERO — full-bleed Flickity carousel of the 5 current projects, ~100vh. Each slide: full-width render, dark bottom-left scrim, large white project name (h1, 36px desktop / very large on mobile), 3-line description, sharp-cornered solid-orange uppercase CTA. Pagination dots bottom-centre-left: active dot is a wide orange pill/bar, inactive are small grey circles. Autoplays every 3s, wraps around, pauses on hover. No prev/next arrows on desktop.

OVERLAPPING VIDEO CARD — a tall white card is absolutely positioned so it straddles the hero/next-section boundary at the right third, with a thin orange bar capping its top edge, small grey 'click here' kicker, larger dark label, and a big circular outline play button. Opens a YouTube video (currently gated behind the marketing-cookie placeholder).

ABOUT COMPANY — two-column: left = uppercase section title + body paragraph on a very light grey panel; right = the video card. Below it a row of 3 animated statistic counters (years / families / completed complexes) built as odometer digit reels.
'WHY US' STRIP — full-width dark/imagery band with an uppercase heading and supporting copy, edge-to-edge photography.

CURRENT PROJECTS — a tall (~3200px) stacked sequence of project rows. Each row is a full-bleed render with a text block (project name, short description, 'see details' link) and the whole card is wrapped in a single <a>; the image scales 1.1 on card hover inside an overflow-hidden frame.
INTERIOR DESIGN — service block with heading, paragraph, and a set of masked interior photos (some inside 3D-tilt image frames with data-hover3d).

COMPLETED PROJECTS — a Flickity carousel (6 finished complexes) with shaped centre-middle prev/next arrows and small round dots underneath; each cell is a render + uppercase name + description + 'see details'.

LEAD FORM SECTION — 'request an offer' Contact Form 7 block on a light panel: two-column field grid (name / phone / email / message), GDPR acceptance checkbox with a custom orange-outlined tick, orange submit button, invisible reCAPTCHA.
OUR STORY — narrative text block paired with imagery.

GOOGLE REVIEWS — third-party Google Reviews widget: aggregate 4.6 star badge, review count, 'powered by Google' mark, horizontally scrollable review cards with avatars, star rows, relative dates and a 'read more' expander.
VIDEO / MARKETING EMBED — a 550px full-width YouTube block, replaced by a Complianz consent placeholder until marketing cookies are accepted.

FOOTER (very tall, ~2400px, 7 columns/rows): two phones, email, address, Facebook/Instagram icon row, business hours, a repeated menu column (home / careers / contacts), legal links (terms, privacy, cookies), and a design-studio credit line.

PERSISTENT CHROME: (a) vertical left sticky tab rotated with writing-mode:vertical-lr that opens the 'request an offer' modal; (b) vertical right sticky tab holding a rotated burger/side-drawer trigger; both slide off-canvas horizontally when the header hides, and are display:none on mobile. (c) Chaty floating orange chat bubble bottom-right with a white tooltip pill and a spin/rotate morph between open and close icons. (d) Complianz cookie modal on first load with Accept / Refuse / Preferences.
layoutPatterns: Elementor flex containers (e-con) on a 1140px max site width; sections alternate white and a very light neutral grey (#EDEFF2 / #E1E3E6 family) with occasional full-bleed dark or photographic bands.
Alternating full-bleed photography and boxed text — nearly every project row is edge-to-edge imagery with the copy inset, so the page reads as a stack of wide cinematic bands rather than a card grid.

Deliberate overlap: the white video card breaks the hero's bottom boundary and sits half over the next section, with a thin orange rule capping it — the single strongest compositional move on the page.
Zero border-radius on buttons and most panels; corners are hard. Small radius only on third-party widgets (reviews, chat).
Vertical rotated sticky rails on both screen edges (writing-mode: vertical-lr + rotate) create a framed 'gallery' feel and keep the offer CTA permanently on screen.

Fullscreen overlay menu is a 3-zone layout on a dark charcoal ground with 1px hairline column rules: [Meniu links] | [Current projects list + Completed projects list] | [2x2 grid of project image cards with a light caption bar under each].
Hero text is bottom-left anchored over a gradient scrim rather than centred — leaves the render's subject visible on the right.
Apartment drill-down is a strict 4-level URL hierarchy: /project/ -> /blocul-N/ -> /etajul-X-Y/ -> /apartamentul-Z/, each level a full page with its own interactive image.

Apartment detail page layout: hero (unit ID + area + 'download tech sheet' PDF button) -> room-by-room technical breakdown list with m2 per room and a total -> inline lead form -> 'other apartments' carousel -> footer.
Floor plans on mobile use a forced-overflow horizontal scroll region (width:150%/250% + white-space:nowrap) with a written 'swipe left/right' hint.
Generous vertical rhythm but a very small body type size (12px paragraphs) against large uppercase section headings — a wide type-size gap rather than a smooth scale.
animations: SMART STICKY HEADER — on first stick the header snaps to translateY(-100%), then a keyframe 'stickySlideOut' (0.4s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)) hides it on scroll-down and 'stickySlideDown' (0.65s, same easing) brings it back on scroll-up. The utility top bar is tagged lqd-hide-onstuck and disappears with it; the logo shrinks in the stuck state.

STICKY EDGE RAILS — the left 'request an offer' tab and right burger rail transition transform 1.25s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) (opacity 0.3s with 0.3s delay); when the header hides they translate(-100%) / translate(100%) off the left and right edges, and slide back with a 0.15s stagger.

HERO CAROUSEL — Flickity: wrapAround true, autoPlay 3000ms, pauseAutoPlayOnHover true, cellAlign 'left', pageDots true, prevNextButtons false. Slides push horizontally (translate3d on the flickity-slider track) rather than fade; adjacent slides are visible mid-transition, which reads as a filmstrip push.
SECOND CAROUSEL (completed projects) — Flickity with wrapAround, prevNextButtons true using 'navArrow 4' shaped arrows appended inside the container at centre-middle, plus small round style-1 dots.

DOT STATES — active dot morphs from a small grey circle into a wide orange pill (style4 / lg). Other dot styles in the theme scale 1.35x and draw a 3px ring via a ::before scaling 0.5 -> 1 over 0.3s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1).

ODOMETER COUNTERS — the killer detail. Each statistic renders an invisible sizing span plus an overflow-hidden mask containing a <ul> of the digits 0-9; GSAP translates the list on Y (e.g. transform: translate3d(0, -369.577%, 0)) so digits roll like a slot machine into place. Driven by data-enable-counter + data-counter-options={targetNumber}.

FULLSCREEN NAV OPEN — a multi-layer choreographed wipe: (1) the overlay fades in 0.15s (on close it waits 0.8s so the wipe can play out); (2) the background is built from 4 column panels plus 2 side panels, each containing a span that animates transform: scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1) over 0.65s cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1) with a 50ms delay — a left-to-right column wipe; (3) each column's 1px hairline rule (::before, rgba(0,0,0,.1), transform-origin center top) animates scaleY(0) -> scaleY(1) over 0.75s with a 0.25s delay, so vertical grid lines draw downward; (4) the menu content container animates clip-path polygon from a zero-width sliver to full over 2s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) with 0.15s delay — a slow left-to-right content reveal; (5) the fixed close X fades in at 0.6s delay. Menu links are set at font-size 4.5vw / weight 700 / line-height 1.1.

BURGER MORPH — .nav-trigger bars transition 0.3s; on activation the outer bars fade and translate together while the middle bar rotates 45deg (with a ::before rotated -90deg) to form an X, using cubic-bezier(.65,.05,.36,1) with 0.1-0.2s internal delays so the bars collapse then the cross rotates.

SUBMENU REVEAL — .nav-item-children go from opacity 0 / translateY to visible over 0.85s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1); inside the fullscreen nav they open sideways at left:110% sliding from translate(-10px).
PROJECT CARD IMAGE ZOOM — .coloana{overflow:hidden} with .coloana:hover .img-hover-proiecte{transform:scale(1.1)} over 0.4s ease; the whole card is the anchor so the crop is the hover affordance.

3D TILT — two image groups carry data-hover3d="true" on a .perspective wrapper with .transform-style-3d inner and data-stacking-factor="1" on the figure: mouse position drives a rotateX/rotateY tilt with the inner layers offset for parallax depth. Base transition on .lqd-imggrp-single is transform 0.65s cubic-bezier(.05,.7,.2,1).

LAZY IMAGE FADE — every content image ships as an inline SVG data-URI placeholder with data-src/data-srcset/data-aspect; .ld-lazyload{opacity:.0001; transition:opacity 1s} then .loaded{opacity:1}. A slow 1s cross-fade as each render decodes, driven by IntersectionObserver.

BUTTON HOVERS (theme library, partially used) — .btn-solid:hover lifts translateY(-2px) with a 0 12px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.12) shadow and swaps to the primary colour; .btn-underlined draws a ::after underline via scaleX(0)->1 with transform-origin flipping from right to left on hover (0.3s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)); .btn-hover-reveal slides an icon in while pushing the label (0.5s cubic-bezier(0,.71,.4,1)); .btn-hover-swp cross-swaps two icons with staggered 0.225s delays; .btn-icon-ripple runs an infinite 2s expanding ring; .btn-hover-txt-switch-x/y slides the label out and a duplicate (attr(data-text)) in; .btn-hover-txt-marquee-x/y loops the label infinitely; .btn-hover-txt-liquid-x/y animates per-character with a calc(var(--chars-index)*30ms) stagger.

MODAL / LIGHTBOX — custom Lity build (.lqd-lity): opacity+visibility 0.3s, fixed close button with backdrop-filter: blur(3px), overscroll-behavior contained content pane. Used for the 'request an offer' popup and for full-size floor-plan images (Fresco skin on a white background).

IMAGE MAP HOTSPOT HOVER — Image Map Pro polygons transition all properties: fill orange #ff6600 at background_opacity 0 -> 0.4 on hover, with a persistent 0.75-opacity orange stroke. Tooltip animation is 'grow' (scale-up) on the complex-level map, sticky (follows the cursor) there and static on the deeper maps; show_tooltips is 'mouseover'.

CHAT WIDGET — Chaty bubble: the main icon rotates 540deg and fades out while the close icon rotates 180deg in; the tooltip pill fades/slides; there is a chaty-animation-spin class on the button and an exit-intent overlay that reveals with clip-path: circle(100%).
SMOOTH SCROLL — html { scroll-behavior: smooth } so all in-page anchors ease rather than jump.
PAGE TRANSITION — Elementor Pro's <e-page-transition> is styled (background #FFBC7D) in the kit but is NOT active on the live page.

NOT PRESENT (important): despite GSAP 3.12.5, ScrollTrigger and SplitText all being loaded, ScrollTrigger.getAll() returns 0 and there are zero data-reveal / data-split-text / data-custom-animations / data-parallax elements. There are no scroll-triggered reveals, no text splitting, no parallax, no pinning, no counters-on-scroll beyond the odometer, and no cursor effects (lqd-cc-label-trigger classes exist on 12 elements but no custom cursor element is rendered). The libraries are loaded and unused.
result.typography: "Single family throughout: Inter (self-hosted via liquid-local-fonts), with Roboto / Roboto Slab declared as Elementor global tokens but overridden. Very compressed scale with a big jump between headings and body: h1 36px/600 (white on hero, 43.2px line-height); h2 28px/500 uppercase in the dark neutral #3A3839 with a loose 42px line-height; h3 16px/600 uppercase; h4 20px/400; body 16px/400 with a very airy 29.44px line-height; paragraphs inside content blocks drop to 12px/18px; buttons 12px/700 uppercase, 14.52px line-height. Letter-spacing is 'normal' everywhere — no tracking work at all, which is the single biggest typographic weakness. Uppercase is the section-title device (h2/h3) while hero titles stay sentence case. Links are brand orange #FF6600, dimming to rgba(255,102,0,.85) on hover."
result.imageryStyle: "Almost entirely full-bleed architectural CGI renders and drone-style photography of finished complexes — golden-hour skies, cars and greenery in frame, warm-neutral facades that echo the orange accent. Images run edge-to-edge with no rounded corners and no duotone or colour treatment; contrast is managed with a dark linear scrim behind hero text rather than by filtering the image. Aspect ratios are wide 16:9-ish for hero and project bands, portrait-ish (580x862) for floor plans and gallery items, 2:1 for card thumbnails. Interior-design photos appear inside 3D-tilt frames. Floor plans are flat PNG line drawings on white, opened full-size in a white-background lightbox. Building/complex artboards for the picker are 1920x1080 JPEGs. Every image is served as an SVG placeholder first, with data-aspect reserving the box so there is no layout shift, then cross-fading in over 1s."
result.buildingOrUnitPicker:
"YES — a full 4-level drill-down built on the Image Map Pro WordPress plugin v6.0.18 (/wp-content/plugins/image-map-pro/js/client/main.js), exposed as window.ImageMapPro with an instances registry keyed by map name. It is SVG-polygon hotspots over a raster render, NOT 3D and NOT a filterable inventory.

LEVEL 1 — COMPLEX MAP (on the project page, e.g. /proiecte-curente/grenoble-residence/, sitting right under the page title as a full-width band). Artboard is a 1920x1080 aerial render of the whole complex (Complex-opt.jpg). Four <svg class="imp-object-poly imp-object"> polygons are absolutely overlaid, one per building. Default style: fill #ff6600 at background_opacity 0 (fully invisible), stroke #ff6600 at 0.75 opacity, stroke-width 0, so at rest the render is completely clean with no visible outlines. On MOUSEOVER: background_opacity animates 0 -> 0.4 (transition: all), i.e. the building silhouette glows translucent orange, and a dark tooltip with an orange arrow (border-top-color rgba(255,104,0,1)) appears next to the cursor showing only the block name ('Blocul 1'..'Blocul 4'). Tooltip config: enable_tooltips true, show_tooltips 'mouseover', sticky_tooltips true (follows the cursor), tooltip_animation 'grow' (scales up). On CLICK: actions.click = 'follow-link' to /proiecte-curente/grenoble-residence/blocul-N/ in the same window. Zoom is configured but disabled (enable_zooming false, zoom_on_object_click false, zoom buttons true, max_zoom 4, hold_ctrl_to_zoom true). Navigator off. objectConfig has glowing_objects false and pageload_animation 'none', so nothing pulses to advertise that the render is clickable.

LEVEL 2 — FLOOR PICKER (/blocul-1/). Artboard is a 1920x1080 straight-on facade render (tronson-1-1.jpg) with 13 horizontal polygon bands stacked up the building: 'Parter', 'Etajul 1' through 'Etajul 11', and 'Penthouse'. Same interaction: invisible at rest, orange fill at 0.4 opacity plus a name tooltip on hover, follow-link on click. Tooltips here are constrained to the container and tooltip_animation is 'none' (instant). Note that all typical floors 1-11 link to one shared '/etajul-1-11/' page, so only Parter and Penthouse are genuinely distinct destinations.

LEVEL 3 — FLOOR PLATE (/etajul-1-11/). Artboard is a flat PNG floor plan (plan_etaj_1.png) with 9 apartment polygons. Crucially the fill here is BLACK (#000000) and the per-unit default background_opacity varies: 0 for one unit, 0.4 for most, ~0.60 for two. That varying dark scrim is the only availability signalling on the whole site — there is no legend, no colour key, no free/reserved/sold states, no price and no label rendered on the plate. Hover raises every polygon to 0.4 black; click follows to the apartment page. Tooltips are set to fullscreen on mobile only.

LEVEL 4 — APARTMENT PAGE (/apartamentul-1/). No image map. Layout: hero with unit identifier and area ('Ap. 1 (1 odaie), suprafata 41,64 m2') plus a 'download technical sheet' PDF button; a room-by-room technical breakdown listing every room with its m2 and a total plus room count; an inline 'request an offer' form; an 'other apartments' carousel of six unrelated units; footer. Floor-plan images open in a Fresco/Elementor lightbox on a white background. There is no price, no floor/orientation selector, no availability badge, no favourites, no compare and no back-link to the floor plate.

SUPPORTING UI: Image Map Pro's object_list is enabled (menu_position 'right', menu_style 'on-top', flat_hierarchy true, search disabled) but the child theme hides it on desktop (.imp-ui-light .imp-object-menu-right{display:none}) and only shows it under 768px as a burger-triggered list, with the burger repositioned to the left. On mobile the floor plans additionally live inside a forced horizontal-scroll strip (.bloc-scroll-orizontal-planimetrii{width:250%; white-space:nowrap}) with a written 'swipe left/right to see the floor plans' hint. A parallel Flickity/Elementor tab widget on the project page filters apartment cards by delivery semester ('Semestrul 1 2024' ... 'Semestrul 2 2026'). The same Image Map Pro pattern is reused on their satulgerman.solomon.md sister site."
result.techStack: "WordPress on LiteSpeed with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9. Page built with Elementor 4.2.3 + Elementor Pro 4.2.2 (flex containers / e-con, Theme Builder header & footer). Theme: 'Hub' by LiquidThemes with a 'hub-child' child theme; all custom widgets carry the lqd-/ld- prefix (hub_fancy_heading, ld_fancy_image, ld_button, ld_carousel, ld_counter, ld_modal_window, ld_custom_menu, ld_fullscreen_nav, ld_header_sidedrawer, ld_header_trigger, ld_header_image, ld_cf722, ld_tabs) plus the hub-elementor-addons plugin. Animation/UI libraries loaded from the theme: GSAP 3.12.5 + ScrollTrigger + SplitText (SplitText and ScrollTrigger are loaded but produce zero instances on the live page), Flickity + flickity-fade for all carousels, jQuery 3.7.1 + jquery-migrate + jQuery UI, Bootstrap (collapse/toggle used for the nav), fastdom, imagesLoaded, a custom lazyload.min.js, fontfaceobserver, an IntersectionObserver polyfill, tinycolor, Fresco and Lity lightboxes (theme-skinned as lqd-lity). Interactive building maps: Image Map Pro for WordPress 6.0.18. Other plugins: TranslatePress Multilingual 3.3.3 (RO/EN/RU), Contact Form 7 6.1.7 + wpcf7-redirect + invisible reCAPTCHA v2, Chaty Pro 3.1.7 (floating multi-channel chat), Complianz GDPR (consent banner + marketing-content blocking with generated placeholders), Widget for Google Reviews 6.9.11, Google Tag Manager (GTM-54NRT53) and a Facebook pixel. Fonts self-hosted locally (liquid-local-fonts: Inter, Roboto, Roboto Slab). Homepage HTML is ~543KB and the DOM is ~16,800px tall — heavy."
whatMakesItFeelPremium: The overlapping white video card that straddles the hero boundary with a thin orange rule capping its top — one confident compositional break in an otherwise rectilinear stack, and the cheapest way to make a template feel art-directed.

Odometer/slot-machine counters: an overflow-hidden mask over a 0-9 digit list translated on Y by GSAP. Reads far more expensive than a plain count-up and is trivially reusable for 'years / units delivered / families housed'.

The fullscreen menu's layered wipe: white column panels scaling in on X (0.65s), hairline column rules drawing down on Y (0.75s, 0.25s delay), then the whole content block revealed by a 2s clip-path polygon sweep. Three staggered mechanics on three different properties in one gesture — copy this wholesale.
Menu links sized in viewport units (4.5vw, weight 700, line-height 1.1) so the overlay always feels poster-scale regardless of screen size.
Smart-sticky header with distinct out and back easings and durations (0.4s out / 0.65s in, both cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)) — the asymmetry is what makes it feel considered rather than mechanical.
Vertical rotated sticky rails on both edges (writing-mode: vertical-lr) that slide off-canvas horizontally when the header hides — keeps a permanent conversion CTA on screen without a floating pill.
Zero-radius, uppercase, letterspaced orange CTAs against warm architectural renders — the hard-edged geometry reads as construction/engineering rather than generic SaaS.

Restraint at rest on the building map: hotspots are 100% invisible until hover, so the render is never defaced by outlines. The 0 -> 0.4 orange fill plus a cursor-following tooltip is all the affordance it uses.
Whole-card anchors with overflow-hidden frames and a 1.1x image scale on hover (0.4s ease) — one CSS rule, and it makes a plain project list feel interactive.
Aspect-ratio-reserved lazy loading (SVG data-URI placeholder + data-aspect + a 1s opacity cross-fade) so nothing jumps and renders arrive like a slow dissolve rather than a pop.
Consistent single-typeface discipline (Inter only) with a large size gap between uppercase section titles and small body copy — restrained even where the rest of the build isn't.
The 4-level URL hierarchy (/project/block/floor/apartment/) — each step is a real, shareable, indexable page, which is better for SEO and for sales staff sending links than a single JS app state.
weaknesses: Almost no motion where it matters. GSAP, ScrollTrigger and SplitText are all loaded and shipped, yet ScrollTrigger.getAll() is 0 and there are zero data-reveal / data-split-text / data-parallax elements. Nothing enters on scroll — sections just appear. Pamir can beat this trivially and should not copy the emptiness.

Payload without payoff: 543KB of HTML, jQuery + jQuery UI + Bootstrap + GSAP + three lightbox libraries, most of it unused. The lqd-highlight-classic class is on 75 headings but the inner span the effect needs is never rendered — dead markup.

The building/apartment picker gives no commercial information at all: no price, no availability status, no legend, no floor/orientation, no unit labels drawn on the plate. Availability is implied only by three different black-scrim opacities (0 / 0.4 / 0.6) with nothing telling the visitor what they mean.

No cross-project unit search or filter. The header's primary 'choose an apartment' CTA just dumps the visitor on a project list; there is no filter by rooms, area, floor, budget or delivery date, no sort, no favourites, no compare.

The picker has no back-navigation or breadcrumb — once on an apartment page you cannot step back to the floor plate or the building, and the 'other apartments' carousel shows unrelated units from other blocks.
Floors 1-11 all collapse into one shared page, so the eleven floor hotspots are a lie — clicking any of them lands on the same content.

Nothing signals that the render is clickable: glowing_objects is false and pageload_animation is 'none', so a first-time visitor has to discover the hotspots by accident. At minimum add a one-time pulse or an always-on faint outline.
Zero letter-spacing anywhere and a jarring type scale (12px body paragraphs sitting under 28px uppercase headings) — the typography is set, not designed.
Hero carousel autoplays every 3 seconds with no progress indicator and no pause control, which is too fast to read the description and steals agency.
Mobile floor plans rely on a hacked 250%-wide overflow-scroll region plus a written 'swipe' instruction instead of proper pinch-zoom or a fitted viewer.
A 2400px tall footer with seven stacked blocks that duplicates the main menu and the contact details already present in the header and the topbar.

Third-party widgets break the visual system: the Google Reviews block and the Chaty bubble bring their own radii, blues, shadows and type, and the Complianz consent gate leaves a grey placeholder card where the main video should be.
The consent modal blocks the entire hero on first load with no visible page behind it — the first impression of the site is a grey dialog.

Accessibility gaps: *:focus { outline: none !important } is set globally in the child theme; hotspots are bare SVG polygons with no keyboard focus, no roles and no accessible names; the odometer digit lists expose all ten digits to assistive tech.

Leftover/contradictory tokens in the stylesheet (--color-primary #184341 dark teal from the theme demo fighting the real brand #FF6600, a button colour declared twice as #F40000 then #EB711D) and a literal syntax error in the child CSS (a stray ')' in the .imp-ui-top-right rule) — signs of an unmaintained build.
